candidates.name: Subacute Thyroiditis
support_spans: pain starting 5–6 days after each shot
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms and lab results, including the extremely low TSH level and elevated ESR, are consistent with subacute thyroiditis, which can be triggered by the COVID-19 vaccine.

candidates.name: Thyroiditis due to Autoimmune Response
candidates.why: The patient's low TSH level and presence of thyroid peroxidase antibodies, although low, could suggest an autoimmune thyroiditis, but the absence of higher antibody levels makes this less likely.

candidates.name: Graves' Disease
candidates.why: The patient's low TSH and elevated T3 and T4 levels could suggest Graves' disease, but the lack of significant thyroid peroxidase antibodies and the clinical context make this less likely.

key_evidence_spans: pain starting 5–6 days after each shot

candidates.name: Subacute Thyroiditis
support_spans: TSH <0.0005 IU/mL (prior TSH 2.03 IU/mL one week before vaccination)
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms and lab results, including a significantly decreased TSH level and elevated ESR, are consistent with subacute thyroiditis, which can be triggered by the COVID-19 vaccine.
candidates.protected_reason: This diagnosis may be easily missed due to its rarity and the fact that it can be triggered by a recently administered vaccine, making it a potential counter-anchor diagnosis.

candidates.name: Thyroiditis due to Autoimmune Thyroid Disease
support_spans: TSH <0.0005 IU/mL (prior TSH 2.03 IU/mL one week before vaccination)
candidates.why: Although the patient has no history of thyroid disease, the presence of thyroiditis and significantly decreased TSH level could suggest an autoimmune thyroid disease, which may have been previously undiagnosed.
candidates.protected_reason: This diagnosis may deserve minority protection due to the potential for autoimmune thyroid disease to be underdiagnosed or misdiagnosed, particularly in patients without a prior history of thyroid disease.

mildly enlarged left paratracheal lymph nodes
contradict_spans: no history of head or neck radiation, or family history of head and neck cancer
candidates.why: The presence of heterogeneous masses in both thyroid lobes and mildly enlarged lymph nodes could suggest a rare diagnosis such as thyroid lymphoma, which may not be immediately considered due to its low prevalence.
